key_insight: Predicting an adversary’s next move requires tracking both its current behavioral mode and which actions are possible now. This paper uses a hidden Markov model to represent modes that persist but can switch during an episode.
problem_solved: A defender needs next-action probabilities using only information available before the action occurs, despite changing attacker behavior and state-dependent action arguments.
method: Represent the attacker’s active behavioral regime as a hidden Markov state.
Model regime persistence and switches within an episode.
Use regime-conditioned action probabilities while accounting for operations and their changing feasible arguments.
impact: The approach offers a structured way to anticipate adversary actions when behavior and available choices evolve. The supplied abstract is truncated, so empirical performance and implementation details cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Hidden-state timeline showing persistent behavioral regimes and switch points.
Transition diagram connecting latent regimes to observable actions.
Action tree separating operations from state-dependent feasible arguments.
Prediction schematic: available information → model → next-action probability distribution.
paper_title: A Hidden Markov Preference Model for Online Prediction of Adversary Actions
paper_authors: Angel Daruna, Michael Cogswell, Tixiao Shan, Yi Yao, Han-Pang Chiu
